name: LegalHold
purpose: Suspends retention-driven deletion and erasure cascades for records covered by a litigation or regulatory hold until the hold is released.
api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class LegalHold:
    hold_id: str
    scope_query: str
    opened_at: datetime
    opened_by: str

class LegalHoldRegistry(Protocol):
    def open(self, hold: LegalHold) -> None: ...
    def release(self, hold_id: str, released_by: str) -> None: ...
    def covers(self, record_id: str) -> bool: ...
invariants: RetentionPolicy.sweep and DataSubjectRequest erasure MUST call covers(record_id) before deletion; deletion of held records is FORBIDDEN.
Opening and releasing a hold MUST each emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry with actor and scope.
A hold CANNOT be silently released; release requires a distinct released_by actor from opened_by or an explicit override flag.
Held records MUST remain readable to authorized investigators; indexes SHALL NOT drop held rows.
scope_query MUST be stable against schema evolution; unresolved fields SHALL raise on open rather than silently miss records.
extension_contract: Storage adapters implement a HoldCheck hook that intercepts delete operations. Target applications extend the registry with custom scope resolvers (e.g. tenant_id = X) by subclassing the scope query evaluator and registering it.
consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timezone

hold = LegalHold(
    hold_id='case-2024-1138',
    scope_query="tenant_id = 'acme' AND created_at >= '2023-01-01'",
    opened_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
    opened_by='counsel@acme.com',
)
registry.open(hold)
assert registry.covers('user:42') in (True, False)

sources.source: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, 2022 revision)
sources.locator: CC2.3 — internal communication about obligations; evidence preservation
AU-11 Audit Record Retention — preservation for investigations

why_essential: Without an explicit hold primitive, the retention sweeper destroys evidence under active litigation and the erasure endpoint fulfills an RTBF request that should have been paused; one flag cannot carry that logic.
alternatives_considered: A boolean column 'do_not_delete' — no scope, no audit, no release protocol.
Disabling the purge job globally — over-broad, violates retention for unrelated data.
Email-based legal notice to ops — not enforceable in code.
